record.paper_title: Some problems and conjectures about L2-invariants
record.original_question: Let F be a field with Q ⊆ F ⊆ C, and let G be a group whose finite subgroups have bounded order. If lcm(G) denotes the least common multiple of the orders of the finite subgroups of G, must every finitely presented FG-module M satisfy the integrality condition lcm(G) · dim_{N(G)}(N(G) ⊗_{FG} M) ∈ Z? Equivalently, when G is torsionfree, are the resulting L2-Betti numbers always integers?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1 (Atiyah Conjecture). Consider a field F with Q ⊆ F ⊆ C. Let G be a group possessing an upper bound on the orders of its finite subgroups. Let lcm(G) be the natural number given by the least common multiple of the orders of its finite subgroups. We say that G satisfies the Atiyah Conjecture with coefficients in F, if for any finitely presented F G-module M the von Neumann dimension satisfies lcm(G) · dimN(G)(N (G) ⊗F G M) ∈ Z.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field with $\mathbb{Q} \subseteq F \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, and let $G$ be a discrete group such that there is a finite upper bound on the orders of the finite subgroups of $G$. Define $\mathrm{lcm}(G) \in \mathbb{N}$ to be the least common multiple of the orders of the finite subgroups of $G$. Let $\mathcal{N}(G)$ denote the group von Neumann algebra of $G$, equipped with its canonical finite normal trace, and let $\dim_{\mathcal{N}(G)}$ be the associated von Neumann dimension on $\mathcal{N}(G)$-modules. 

Prove or disprove: for every finitely presented left $FG$-module $M$,
$$\mathrm{lcm}(G) \cdot \dim_{\mathcal{N}(G)}\bigl(\mathcal{N}(G) \otimes_{FG} M\bigr) \in \mathbb{Z}.$$

In particular, when $G$ is torsion-free (so $\mathrm{lcm}(G) = 1$), must $\dim_{\mathcal{N}(G)}(\mathcal{N}(G) \otimes_{FG} M)$ be an integer for every finitely presented $FG$-module $M$?
artifact.status_search_result: The Strong Atiyah Conjecture (in the form above, for groups with a bound on the orders of finite subgroups, with arbitrary coefficient field between Q and C) remains open in general. It has been verified for various classes (e.g., Linnell's class C, free-by-elementary-amenable groups, and certain closure classes containing free groups), and the center-valued version has been established for some such classes. However, counterexamples to weaker, unbounded-torsion versions of the conjecture exist (Austin, Grabowski, Pichot–Schick–Żuk), and the bounded-torsion case for torsion-free groups generalizes Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture, which is itself open.

status_evidence.title: Atiyah conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The strong Atiyah conjecture states that lcm(G)·dim_{N(G)}(...) is an integer; it implies Kaplansky's zero divisor conjecture for torsion-free groups.
status_evidence.claim: Strong Atiyah Conjecture as stated is open in general; implies Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture in the torsion-free case.

status_evidence.title: On the center-valued Atiyah conjecture for L2-Betti numbers
status_evidence.snippet: The center-valued Atiyah conjecture is proven for all groups in Linnell's class C, containing free-by-elementary amenable groups.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results: the conjecture is known for several classes of groups.

status_evidence.title: L2-Betti numbers and their analogues in positive characteristic (Jaikin-Zapirain)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys current status of Atiyah conjecture and its open status for general groups with bounded torsion.
